claims.head: Don’t expect many shots
claims.call: The game runs at fewer than the two teams’ usual 78.8 unblocked shots per 60 at 5-on-5.
claims.body: St. Louis’s games average only 78.4 unblocked shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined (28th of 32 for pace); Ottawa’s average 79.2 (26th).

claims.head: One power play bites, one doesn’t
claims.body: Ottawa ranks 13th of 32 for power play, toward the lethal end; St. Louis ranks 32nd, toward the harmless end.
claims.call: Ottawa’s power play creates more per 60 than St. Louis’s.

notes.text: L. Mailloux has not played this season. A. Jiricek is in his usual spot beside P. Broberg. That pair is getting 8:50 a game at 5-on-5, down from 11:56 with Mailloux.
J. Spence has started killing penalties: on the ice for 41% of the team’s shorthanded time in 4 games, up from 4% last season.

OTT.head: Ottawa should have the upper hand
OTT.body: Ottawa has controlled the play far better over recent games and has home ice. St. Louis’s way back in is getting to the dangerous areas.

STL.head: St. Louis faces a real test
STL.body: Ottawa has controlled the play far better over recent games and has home ice. St. Louis’s best way through is getting to the dangerous areas.
